title: Moms who went to pelvic pt, PT or Chiro for debilitating lower back pain, what worked?
text:
Currently 20 weeks. What started as a little back pain has gotten to a point where it’s really affecting my life. Two weeks ago I went to the er because the back spasms felt like labor and I was terrified I was losing the baby- if that helps contextualize how bad this pain is. 

Currently I’m walking one to two miles in the morning at a comfortable pace w a band on, then I do about 20 minutes of lifting alternating between lower and upper (3-4 days a week), hip and leg stretching and yoga, I am using a massage gun and heat therapy together and that seems to help a bit- also hot epsom baths every night. 

All these things together make it better but it seems like no matter what around 3 it starts to hurt so so bad that it hurts to walk and hurts to sit. I have a toddler and my husband works a crazy job where his shifts are always different so I’m solo parenting a lot. This is making me a mean exhausted mom because I’m in so much pain, so I’m spending every night crying and feeling like a failure to her. And that the child in my belly is feeling  all my pain and anxiety. Mom guilt is such a bitch. 

My husband thinks Chrio is woo woo but I found reviews for a local place that specializes in prenatal care and it seems really promising. There’s also my knowledge of pelvic floor or pt therapy. I’m just not sure which route to go but I need help. 

I’d be so grateful for anyone’s experiences to help guide me, thank you in advance.

title: Too excited to sleep!
text:
I’m 37 weeks, at my 36+5 I was 2 cm dilated and 60% effaced! Doc said she’d be surprised if I made it to my due date Jan 28th, today I took a nap and woke up to contractions, not intense or super painful but more than Braxton hicks. For me Braxton hicks don’t hurt but my belly tightens, this started as period like cramps that radiated and eventually it felt like a band around my lower back and belly and cramping like real contractions on and off for about an hour,I went to the bathroom and lost my mucus plug, the contractions died down and became like Braxton hicks again and lasted on and off all day, then they kicked back up to contractions around dinner, I did a pregnancy workout along with my stretches before bed, and now I’m laying here trying so hard to sleep but every cramp/contraction/braxton hicks reminds me of how close I am to labor, I felt something fall out of me, went pee and lost the rest of my mucus plug. I know it could be days/ a couple weeks before the day but I have a feeling it’s gonna happen sooner rather than later especially because of how effaced I am. 

I’m just soooo thrilled, so beyond excited for labor and meeting my girl. I know lying awake with adrenaline and anxiety/ excitement pumping isn’t helping anything lol, not sleep or potential labor but I just can’t settle!! 

Sooo close yet sooo far.

title: 29w and already struggling…How did you all make it through the rest of the third trimester?
text:

The main thing I noticed is that it doesn't slide around as much and I don't have to keep adjusting it.


The velcro is also a lot softer than some of the cheaper belly bands I tried before. Those would sometimes scratch my skin, which drove me a little crazy tbh. This band just feels a bit more comfortable overall, especially when I'm moving around. I checked the tag and it turns out it's from Momcozy.


My friend also shared a few little things that helped her during the later stages of pregnancy, like using a pregnancy pillow at night and doing some gentle stretching during the day. I've been trying to do a bit of prenatal yoga whenever I have the energy for it too. Sometimes those things really do help, but other times I still end up feeling huge and kind of clumsy anyway lol. And the belly band has helped quite a bit, especially on days when I have to stand for longer or go out for walks.


I'm still kinda figuring out what works best for my body though, so I'm really curious, how are you all dealing with the discomfort in the later stages of pregnancy?Any advice is welcome.

my sister is pregnant and I need help figuring out the best nursing bras pls
text:
okay so my sister is pregnant with her first baby and somehow I became the unofficial researcher for everything postpartum related lol. I genuinely thought nursing bras would be one of the easier things to buy but apparently there are like a million different styles and everyone online swears by completely different ones.

been lurking this sub for a bit trying to understand what matters and now I have way more questions than answers.

wireless vs supportive bras: from what I’m understanding, most people say wireless nursing bras are WAY more comfortable, especially early postpartum and for sleeping. but then I also keep seeing comments saying some of the super soft stretchy bras stop giving enough support once milk comes in or if size changes a lot. is there actually a good middle ground where it still feels soft but supportive enough to wear outside the house?

the removable pad debate: why is every review section a war over removable pads 😭 half the people say lightly padded bras are lifesavers for leaks and coverage, the other half say the pads fold into abstract art in the wash and drive them insane. did most people actually end up preferring padded or unlined bras long term?

clip-down nursing access: this might sound dumb but are the one-handed clip bras genuinely easier or is that mostly marketing? I keep imagining my sister trying to figure out tiny clips while exhausted at 3am and it suddenly feels like a bigger deal than I originally thought lol.

fabric confusion: I keep seeing bamboo/modal/cotton/seamless nylon blends come up constantly. some people say stretchy seamless bras are best because your body changes so much during pregnancy and postpartum. others say cotton is cooler and more breathable. my sister already sleeps hot so now I’m trying to figure out whether fabric actually changes comfort that much.

sizing: this part seems genuinely chaotic. a lot of people say not to buy too many bras before birth because size changes a ton after milk comes in. but then others say stretchy bras are forgiving enough that it doesn’t matter. realistically how many nursing bras did people actually use at first?

sleep bras vs daytime bras: do people really end up having separate bras for sleeping, nursing, pumping etc or do most eventually find one comfortable style and basically live in it 24/7 😭

brands: I keep seeing Momcozy, Kindred Bravely, Bodily, Hatch, Bravado mentioned constantly. are those actually worth the hype or are there cheaper ones people ended up liking just as much?

also random practical question: do seamless bras stretch out super quickly after constant washing or do decent ones actually hold up okay? because I already know these things are gonna live in the laundry basket.

sorry for the long post lol. just trying to help my sister avoid panic-buying random nursing bras at 2am and ending up uncomfortable during an already stressful/exhausting phase.

title: De-Influence/Influence Baby Registry (Rough Draft)
text:
I am a FTM in my second tri working on a messy rough draft of my baby registry and am completely overwhelmed. Please brutally influence and de-influence me. I want the best of the best when it comes to safety and quality.

A few things to know about my setup:

1. Gender is a surprise - that’s why you'll see random things in different colors. I threw them on just for myself so I can buy when baby comes, but I plan to start off with neutrals
2. I want to be able to bring the baby to my mom's and MIL's houses and have them watch him/her easily. They don't have car seats so I need an infant carrier that is ultra-lightweight for them to hold, simple to install baseless in their cars and easy to click onto our stroller with adapters.
3. We live in Miami, so we aren't going to be offloading a ton of massive gear constantly. We need lightweight and breathable gear that can handle the heat/humidity and neighborhood strolls, but folds up tight

Please tell me what is necessary and what I am missing from these major duplicates so I can trim this list and perfect it. Thank you so much!

**Edit: I know this looks like overconsumption at its finest, but I’m actually here to** ***avoid*** **overconsumption. If I were planning on buying everything (or even half of it), I wouldn't be asking Reddit what to cut. This has been one of the few places where I can get candid opinions from parents instead of sponsored content. So reminder to please be kind!** 

**Edit: We’re doing it guys! I have since removed the baby food maker, the bottle warmer, the different sized bottles, baby floor and booster seat, the owlet, the pee pads, the Lalo hook on high chair, momcozy breast milk storage bottles, the bathtub filter, tubby Todd newborn gift set, the pattern cotton mat, the tumbling mat, the skip hop.**

**And since there were a lot of comments regarding this - I am putting the pump through insurance but the registry serves as more of list for myself to remember to get everything I need and to get feedback on the different brands I've researched (hence the many duplicates especially with the carriers which I have yet to decide on!) A good chunk of the list is set to private so only I can see it and I plan on buying as I go but want to be as prepared as possible so I’m not panicking and doing all this research postpartum.**

**Also, considering Elimination Communication.  Has anyone here actually done this from the get-go? How did it go for you? Is it worth the effort, or should I just stick to regular diapering at first? Thank you!**
